full_judgment: 8. In the face of the language of section 88 of the Bengal Tenancy Act as pointed out above mere presumption for non-production of dakhilas showing payment of rent of the undivided holding will not be sufficient to deprive the pre-emptess from pleading that the alleged order of separation of the holding was not valid, and as such the same was not binding upon the co-shares. I do not find any substance in the contention also. So far the question of estoppel is concerned, I do not find any substance in this point also, simple answer is that there is no estoppel against statute. Mr. Aziz, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee opposite parties referred me to a decision of the Bombay High Court, in the case of Lady Dibai Dinshaw Peti & others Vs. The Dominion of India and another reported in A.I.R 1951 Bombay 72. It appears from this decision that a Division Bench of the Bombay High Court consisting of Chagla, C.J. and bhagwati J. has held that “no person be precluded from pleading that certain orders are illegal or invalid, because the question as to whether orders are illegal or invalid or invalid is a pure question of law and there can be no estoppel against law.”
